messages:
aj: heads-up — seeing a ~5% spike in TLS handshake failures for inference endpoints in eu-west-1 since last cert rotation. errors look like 'tls: client hello without SNI' and a bunch of 502/503 from envoy. anyone touched ALB certs last night?
ops-bot: deploy finished: alb-cert-rotation v2 -> eu-west-1 at 2025-02-12T02:15Z
maya: that was me — we consolidated certs into a single wildcard (*.inference.redwood.ai) to simplify ACM rotation across zones. expected no user-visible change.
lee: quick note: ALB uses SNI to pick which cert to present. if a client doesn't send SNI it gets the default cert, which can break Host-based routing at the app layer. older SDKs sometimes omit SNI.
aj: we have logs from envoy: 'tls: client hello without SNI' then a downstream 503. also a subset of traffic is failing mTLS flows (401).
elena: remember we terminate TLS at ALB (HTTPS listener) and forward plaintext to pods. That means ALB sees client hello and picks cert; it also means we cannot perform mTLS validation at the pods because client certs are terminated at ALB and not forwarded.
maya: right — customers who expect mutual TLS to be validated by our ingress will break if ALB is terminating TLS. For them, we must do TLS passthrough to the ingress (NLB) or use TLS target groups with re-encryption and client cert forwarding if possible.
lee: reproducible test: try openssl s_client with and without -servername.
```bash
openssl s_client -connect inference-eu-west.elb.amazonaws.com:443 -servername app.customer.example -showcerts
```
If you omit -servername you usually get the ALB default cert (wildcard) instead of the host cert.
aj: I tried curl without Host/SNI and ALB served the wildcard cert; our app rejects because Host header != cert SAN -> 400. For mTLS customers we see 401 since client certs never reach envoy.
elena: proposal: for customers using mTLS, spin up an NLB passthrough target for their host so envoy can do TLS termination and validate client cert chains. We'll need one per customer or per tenant group.
maya: downside: NLB removes ALB L7 features (WAF, redirects). Also ACM cert rotation isn't applied the same way. Could we instead configure ALB listener to forward TCP/TLS to targets (protocol TLS) so the target sees TLS? Not sure ALB ever does true passthrough — I think it still terminates for cert selection.
lee: correct — ALB can do TLS to target (re-encrypt) but it still inspects client hello to select the cert via SNI. For true passthrough you need NLB w/ TLS passthrough.
aj: suggested actions:
- aj: add a small test that reproduces client without SNI and gather client IPs/SDK versions.
- maya: map active customers relying on mTLS and mark as impacted.
- elena: spike NLB passthrough setup for one impacted customer and test policy.
- lee: prepare rollback plan for the wildcard cert rotation (ACM fallback) if customer impact > threshold.
maya: created a runbook note and tagged @aj oncall with checklist.
aj: I'll run openssl and post the raw output here shortly.
lee: seeing related alerts: routing-slo-eu triggered for increased 502/503 around the same timeframe. seems correlated to the cert rollout.
ops-bot: alert: routing-slo-eu spike 502 (2025-02-12T02:30Z) — runbook: https://confluence.internal/redwood/runbooks/alb-sni-issues
aj: if anyone needs me to revert the ACM changes I can flip the ALB to the previous cert (fallback) to buy time. ping me.
elena: also note: ALB does not forward client cert details to targets in any header. for mTLS flows we must terminate at envoy to access subject info.
maya: agreed. will sync with infra tomorrow 09:00 PT to propose either per-customer NLB or a hybrid (ALB for general traffic + NLB for mTLS tenants).
aj: thanks — I'll post the openssl logs and list of affected IP ranges once I have them.
